claims.statement: For every 2<=r,s<=20, the polynomial F_r(z) B_s(z)^q with F_r=((1+z)^(r-1)-1)/z and B_s=(1+z)^s+z has finite-order ULC for at least one q in {1,2,3,4}; the least such q occurs 273, 80, 7, and 1 times for q=1,2,3,4, respectively, in the exact census.
claims.scope: Bounded coefficient computation only: 2<=r,s<=20 and q<=4, with exact coefficients, least finite ULC orders, and blocking indices recorded in the replayed census. No conclusion beyond this finite grid or about trees.
claims.reason: retained: Independent exact-integer replay completed all 1,444 cases, reproduced the least-q distribution (273, 80, 7, 1), and passed the pinned 121-row comparison. The normalized finite-ULC criterion and least-order formula are valid, including orders greater than degree. This disposition covers only the bounded coefficient claim and does not establish a family, graph, selector, or tree bridge.

limitations: The review confirms only the finite equal-type grid 2<=r,s<=20 and q<=4.
No uniform absorption result, mixed-arity result, general convolution application, graph/deletion correspondence, selector propagation, or ordinary-tree aggregate implication was established.
No primary-literature theorem was needed for the finite arithmetic claim.
